t.7.10.1: Then Rāma said to the twice-born sage: "How did those brothers live in the forest, O Brahman, and what kind of austerity did those men of great vows then practise?"
t.7.10.2: Then Agastya spoke there to Rāma, whose mind was composed and restrained; and there those brothers devoted themselves to those various ordinances of dharma.
t.7.10.3: Then Kumbhakarṇa, self-controlled and ever devoted to dharma, practised austerities in the summer season, stationed amid the five fires.
t.7.10.5: Thus ten thousand years passed for him as he strove in dharma and remained firmly established on the path of the virtuous.
t.7.10.4: In the rainy season, drenched by the water of the clouds, he sat in the vīrāsana posture, and in the cold season he always made his dwelling in the midst of the water.
t.7.10.6: But Vibhīṣaṇa, righteous of soul, ever devoted to dharma and pure, stood on one foot for five thousand years.
t.7.10.7: When his vow of austerity was completed, the troops of Apsarases danced, a shower of flowers fell, and the deities too were stirred.
t.7.10.9: Thus for Vibhīṣaṇa too, of restrained self, ten thousand years passed, as though he were dwelling in heaven, in the Nandana grove.
t.7.10.8: For five thousand years he followed the course of the sun, and he stood with his head and arms raised upward, his mind fixed on sacred recitation.
t.7.10.11: Thus nine thousand years passed for him, and nine of his heads had also entered the fire.
t.7.10.10: For ten thousand years Daśānana remained without food, and each time a thousand years were complete, he offered one of his heads into the fire.
t.7.10.13: But the Grandfather, greatly pleased, appeared together with the gods and said, "Child, child, Daśagrīva, I am pleased with you."
t.7.10.12: Then, in the tenth thousand years, when that righteous-souled one was eager to cut off his tenth head, the Grandfather arrived there.
t.7.10.14: Quickly choose, O knower of dharma, the boon that you desire. What wish of yours shall I fulfil today? Your toil has not been in vain.
t.7.10.15: Then Daśagrīva, his inner self overjoyed, bowed his head to the god and spoke in a voice choked with delight.
t.7.10.16: O Blessed One, for living beings there is always no fear other than that of death. There is no enemy equal to death; therefore I choose immortality.
t.7.10.17: O Lord of creatures, may I be forever unslayable by the Suparṇas, Nāgas, Yakṣas, Daityas, Dānavas and Rākṣasas, and by the gods as well.
t.7.10.18: O you who are honored by the immortals, I have no concern regarding other creatures, for all living beings, men and the rest, are mere straw to me.
t.7.10.19: Thus addressed by the rākṣasa Daśagrīva, O Rāma, the righteous-souled Grandsire, together with the gods, spoke these words.
t.7.10.20: This shall indeed be so for you, O bull among Rākṣasas. And hear further an auspicious word from me, who am pleased with you here.
t.7.10.21: The heads which you formerly offered into the fire, O sinless one, shall again be yours, just as they were, O Rākṣasa.
t.7.10.22: When the Rākṣasa Daśagrīva had been addressed thus by the Grandsire, those heads of his that had been offered into the fire rose up again.
t.7.10.23: Having thus spoken to Daśagrīva, O Rāma, Prajāpati, the grandfather of the worlds, then addressed these words to Vibhīṣaṇa.
t.7.10.24: O Vibhīṣaṇa, my child, I am well pleased with you, whose mind is joined to righteousness. O knower of dharma, O you of good vows, choose a boon.
t.7.10.25: But Vibhīṣaṇa, righteous of soul, ever endowed with all virtues as the moon is with its rays, spoke these words with joined palms.
t.7.10.26: O Bhagavān, I have achieved my purpose, since the teacher of the worlds himself is gracious to me. If you are pleased, then hear the boon that is to be granted to me, O you of excellent vows.
t.7.10.27: Whatever thought arises in me, in whatever stages of life here, may each such thought be most devoted to dharma, and each such dharma I uphold.
t.7.10.28: O most noble one, this I regard as the highest boon; for nothing in the world is hard to obtain for those devoted to dharma.
t.7.10.29: Then Prajāpati, well pleased, said to Vibhīṣaṇa: "Even as you are most devoted to righteousness, dear child, so too shall this come to pass."
t.7.10.30: Since your mind does not incline toward adharma, though you were born in the womb of a Rākṣasa, O tormentor of foes, I grant you immortality.
t.7.10.31: But, O subduer of foes, as Prajāpati was granting a boon to Kumbhakarṇa, all the gods, with joined palms, spoke these words to him.
t.7.10.32: A boon should not be granted by you to Kumbhakarṇa just yet, for you know how this evil-minded one terrifies the worlds.
t.7.10.33: In Nandana he has devoured seven Apsarases and ten attendants of Mahendra, O Brahman, and sages and men as well.
t.7.10.35: Thus addressed by the gods, Brahmā, the lotus-born, thought of someone; and, thus thought of, the goddess Sarasvatī came and stood at his side.
t.7.10.34: O you of immeasurable splendour, under the pretext of a boon let delusion be given to him; so there would be welfare for the worlds, and he too would be humbled.
t.7.10.36: Then Sarasvatī, standing at his side with joined palms, spoke these words: “Here I am, come, O god; what task shall I perform?”
t.7.10.37: Then Prajāpati spoke these words to Sarasvatī, who had come to him: “O Vāṇī, become, in the lord of the Rākṣasas, that which the gods desire.”
t.7.10.38: Saying “So be it,” she entered, and then Prajāpati said: “Kumbhakarṇa, O mighty-armed one, choose whatever boon you desire.”
t.7.10.39: But Kumbhakarṇa, having heard those words, spoke this speech: "O God of gods, to sleep for many years is what I desire."
t.7.10.40: Having said to him, "So be it," the Grandsire departed for heaven together with the gods, and the goddess Sarasvatī too, having released him, went to heaven.
t.7.10.41: But the evil-minded Kumbhakarṇa, distressed, reflected: "What sort of word is this, what indeed, that has fallen from my mouth today?"
t.7.10.42: Having thus obtained their boons, all the brothers, blazing with splendour, went to the Śleṣmātaka forest and dwelt there happily.
